text:
Watching twenty short clips on a topic isn't the same as twenty real hours of hands-on practice. This week on Tech Thursday we broke down why depth beats scroll speed for AI fluency.

Follow Layer8Culture if you're building with AI.

GPT-6 Sol, Terra, and Luna just shipped inside GitHub Copilot — and the real story isn't the benchmark chart.

What changed: OpenAI split its flagship model into three sizes, all selectable inside Copilot — Sol for heavy reasoning, Terra for balanced work, Luna for fast and cheap.

What it does: lets you match compute to the actual job instead of defaulting to the biggest model for everything, every time.

Why builders should care: most tasks don't need the heaviest model. Knowing when to reach for Luna instead of Sol is the difference between a fast iteration loop and a slow, expensive one.

Try this: this week, set Copilot's auto-model mode to "efficiency" for quick edits and switch to "intelligence" only when you hit something genuinely hard. Notice the difference.

The bigger signal: AI is moving from one giant prompt box into a workflow with real decisions inside it. Multi-model fluency is becoming the actual skill.

Save this for your AI stack.

text:
Nobody tells you the fastest way to get good at AI has nothing to do with watching more videos about it.

On this week's Tech Thursday we talked about the twenty-hour rule: you don't need to be an expert to start, you need twenty real hours of hands-on reps before you're allowed to have an opinion.

Most people spend twenty minutes across twenty different thirty-second clips and call that research. That's not the same thing.

Here's the actual rule: five hours exploring the tool with no goal, ten hours building one real thing, five hours breaking it and fixing what broke. That's when it clicks.
